notes.text: Never two a's in a row, drawn nondeterministically: a b out of "ok" may stay put or slide into "ok (copy)", which behaves identically. The weakness constraint survives the branching — {ok, just saw a, ok (copy)} is one strongly connected component lying wholly inside F, and {dead} is one lying wholly outside.

Weakness constrains the shape of the automaton, so it survives nondeterminism unharmed — what matters is that no SCC straddles F, not how many choices leave a state. Redirect "dead" back into "ok" and the two components merge into one that straddles F; the app reports that before running and falls back to plain Büchi acceptance.

meta.title: Never two a's, with a needless guess
meta.blurb: A nondeterministic weak automaton for the same safety property as the DWA, with a redundant branch that leaves the SCC constraint intact.
